items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Arthur Duncan was who you are referring to. He was the black tap dancer.

ctx.x: Said on the show that he was a black tap dancer, and she said that this was the first instance of a network show being integrated at all.

Well there were not, still to this day there haven’t been many musical shows that were dedicated to music completely in an hour’s time. And I’d never thought about that, but that’s probably true come to think about it. Arthur Duncan was who you are referring to. He was the black tap dancer. And up until — I think there was another, let’s say a couple of years before — the other band later — Guy Lombardo, Guy Lombardo tried to do the same thing that Lawrence did, but he didn’t go over for some reason. And they’re…
And then I think Ralph Humphreys — were you on the band — Ralph Humphreys, the drummer?
